releases.title: Ironman, the Snail, and Steadier Enemies

entries.text: Added the Creative cheat, which waives every crafting, building and upgrade cost; the button was there before but did nothing.
Added a Mode dropdown to the new-store screen: Classic, Ironman and Snail.
Changed the staff and gardener enemies' attacks to a new motion-captured zombie set.
Changed the Tab handbook and roster to toggle open on a press, with Escape or Tab closing it, so it stays up while you read rather than vanishing the moment you let go.
Changed duct tape's weight to bring it in line with the other crafting materials.
Changed fly mode so jump climbs and crouch descends, and releasing both holds your height.
Changed the standing floor signs to show the Durham catalogue artwork, so they match the framed wall posters instead of showing leftover placeholder art.
Fixed world-generated furniture reappearing at its original spot after being dragged somewhere else.
Fixed an issue where furniture a host shoved or dragged stayed put for guests until it settled, then jumped.
Fixed a joined player's inventory, hotbar, equipment and position being left out of the host's save, so everything they were carrying vanished when the session ended.
Fixed lamps and other lit fixtures going dark for everyone else the moment someone picked them up.
Fixed an issue where punching a sign or another prop with no surface material sprayed blood.
Fixed Durham Spring Water and Durham Breakfast Cereal not counting as water and cereal in recipes.
Fixed enemies that wandered off the walkable ground standing frozen for good instead of finding their way back.
Fixed BoneHead's attacks and every enemy's hit reactions playing with scrambled limbs.
Fixed the heavy staff's ground pound repeating with no cooldown.
Fixed the staff enemies bending their arms and fingers past the pose their attack animations were made with.
Fixed forearms pinching thin at the wrist during enemy attacks and hit reactions.
Fixed the Bone Head winding up a throw that never left its hand.
Fixed the TV Head never firing its spotlight beam; it lined up the shot and gave up every time.
Fixed the pillow armour showing bare checkerboard patches on the arms and legs.
Fixed the metal chestplate spitting an error into the log every time it was worn.
Fixed an issue where dismantling or smashing a container destroyed everything inside it; the contents now spill onto the floor.
Fixed the concrete brick and the loose brick showing up as a grey checkerboard.
Fixed a Join Game button appearing in the main and pause menus that never did anything.
Fixed the Windows mouse pointer appearing next to the in-game cursor while hovering a menu's scroll bar.
Fixed an issue where the music stayed quiet after an enemy that had been chasing you died or wandered out of range.
Fixed an issue where killing an employee or mannequin never ticked the "Put something down" objective.
Fixed a rendering stall caused by store signs with broken mesh bounds.
Fixed an issue where a machine that finished while you were away still showed its jobs as queued, with a Cancel button where Take belonged, until the screen was reopened.
Fixed an issue where vending machines hid everything they sold behind ??? until you had carried coins.
Fixed a crash when a world was torn down while furniture was still being returned to the pool.
Fixed a possible crash when the Janitor's acid pool killed something standing in it.
Fixed the Pit's fire floor, which never set anyone alight: standing in it now burns you, and leaving it lets the burn run out.
Fixed claiming a bed not moving where you respawn, and each player now keeps their own bed.
Fixed open edges over drops of two or more floors, which now get a railing instead of nothing.
Fixed an issue where riding in a trolley filled the view with your own knees and arms.
Fixed an issue on high-DPI desktops where borderless mode ran at a scaled-down resolution that Windows then stretched over the panel, and the resolution list could not offer the real one.
Fixed the Pizza Cutter Lamp giving off no light while equipped.
Fixed an issue where a Store Map tile on a height drop spawned no map stand, leaving the compass marker pointing at nothing.
Removed the combat music state: the day and night beds no longer duck to a whisper and play a sting whenever an enemy spots you.

known_issues.text: Furniture flashes when a drag starts and again when it settles.
Loading a save made after a visit to the Pit sets you on fire on arrival.
Elevators don't respond - pressing the button does nothing, so you can't ride between floors.
Some furniture spawns badly placed - floating near steps, lying down, or facing the wrong way.
Aisle sign lettering and framed photos z-fight at some angles - the text flickers as you walk past.
Railings generate along edges with no drop, and are missing from some real ones.
Eighteen materials across fifteen breakable pieces render flat grey once destroyed.
The menus can feel sluggish and the cursor lags behind the mouse.
Very rarely a guest cannot pick up a piece of furniture that just appeared in front of them.

releases.title: Now With 99.7% Reduced Time Between Patches!

entries.text: Improved menu performance.
Added a ten second confirmation prompt after a display change, which puts the old resolution back if you do not confirm, so an unreadable or off-screen mode can no longer strand you.
Changed the upgrade and dismantle tools to read as Hammer Tool and Screwdriver Tool, so they are not mistaken for the Hammer weapon of the same name.
Changed the dowel bat so its recipe is unlocked from the start instead of needing to be discovered, so there is a weapon to build on the first crafting bench.
Changed the on-screen key prompts so mouse buttons draw as a mouse with the pressed button lit, rather than a box lettered LMB, so a left or right click reads at a glance.
Changed the Controls menu so look speed sits at the top, above the key bindings, instead of below a list long enough to scroll past.
Changed the Video menu so display settings sit at the top, above the graphics quality options, to match where most games put them.
Changed the on-screen action prompts to name what the button actually does, so primary fire reads Attack and the drag prompt appears only while something draggable is in front of you.
Fixed god mode not preventing damage: the cheat menu showed it switched on while the player still took hits and died.
Fixed tools reporting that they equip to a Weapon slot; the recipe panel now calls it the hand slot, which is what weapons, tools and consumables all share.
Fixed duct tape weighing 1kg a roll, ten times heavier than every other crafting material.
Fixed the look-speed slider ignoring click and drag, so the handle now follows the pointer instead of only jumping to where you click.
Fixed the what is new bulletin reappearing every time you returned to the main menu, so it now shows once per update and stays shut after you close it.

Fixed an issue where changing resolution or window mode did not apply correctly: picking a resolution forced the game into fullscreen, the window shrank a little further with every change, and borderless and fullscreen could not be reached from windowed.
Fixed the flashlight switching itself back on a couple of seconds after you turned it off at night, and relighting whenever you took a hit, so it now stays off until the next morning.
Removed the Ghost cheat, which never did anything: it set a flag no part of the game read, and the No Aggro toggle beside it already makes enemies ignore you.

releases.title: A first launch that settles itself

entries.text: A fresh install now warms its shaders behind a setup screen instead of hitching its way through your first session. It ends when the shaders are actually done, not when a timer says so, and tells you what it compiled.
A guest's craft and production orders go through. The host was refusing them and saying nothing - the order simply vanished off the guest's screen.
A launch that could hang on a black screen and never recover, on Nvidia cards. A shader check fired while the upscaler was still starting up and stalled the frame.
The main menu no longer draws the shop behind it. Every frame spent on it went to pixels nobody could see - and on a first boot those frames were taken from the shader compiler.
The inventory character is framed head-to-toe again instead of being scaled up and clipped at the edges of its panel.
Television static is half as loud.

releases.title: The handbook, and a quieter night

entries.text: Hold <kbd>Tab</kbd> for the staff handbook - every objective as a card, with hints, field notes and a live controls page. In co-op the right panel is the shift roster.
The night hazard is gone. It drained 1 health every 8 seconds all night and re-armed the regen block with every bite, so nothing ever healed it back.
Biome ambience is a night-only bed. By day the store plays its jazz and nothing else; the two used to stack and the room tone masked the music.
The flashlight beam stops swinging out of frame on a fast turn, and your own body and worn gear no longer throw a shadow down your own beam.
Guests get the full item catalogue on join - items used to render as raw ids with no description for the whole session.
Dragged furniture moves for guests again. It had been frozen until you let go since 18 Aug.

releases.title: Hits that land, and better defaults

entries.text: Hit reactions are physics-driven: enemies flinch on every hit and go down on a break.
Enemies keep their feet on the floor while attacking, shorten their stride on stairs and slow to a walk on a climb.
A tile decides its enemies while you are still a LOD ring away, instead of after it has already come into view.
